model_annotation: The plot illustrates the loss values for several language models over increasing iterations. The x-axis, labeled "#Iteration", represents a linear scale ranging from 0 to 140000, with tick labels spaced approximately 20000 units apart. The y-axis, labeled "Loss", is also linear and extends from approximately 2.4 to 3.4, with tick intervals of 0.2. A solid red line represents the loss for the “Vanilla” model, initially around 2.8 and decreasing to approximately 2.5 by 140000 iterations. A dashed orange line represents the loss for a StrLMLL model with n=64 iterations, beginning at approximately 2.9 and approaching a value of around 2.7 by 140000 iterations. A solid brown line shows the loss for a SepLLM with n=64 iterations, starting at around 3.0 and decreasing to approximately 2.9 by 140000 iterations. A dotted green line represents the loss for a SepLLM with n=64, H, beginning at approximately 3.1 and reducing to approximately 3.0 by 140000 iterations. A solid magenta line depicts the loss for a SepLLM with n=64, H/T, initially at approximately 3.1 and decreasing to around 2.9 by 140000 iterations. Finally, a solid blue line represents the loss for a SepLLM with n=128 iterations, starting at approximately 3.2 and decreasing to around 2.8 by 140000 iterations.
